name: floti-desktop
instructions: These tools open Floti's views, in the window of Floti, the app hosting this session, so you can show the user what you are talking about instead of describing where to find it. What you open appears beside this session's tab and the keyboard stays in the terminal, so the user can keep typing to you. Floti's views: a file's tab shows a file's text with its changed lines marked, scrolled to a line when you give one - use it to show code you wrote, read or are asking about; the Files view is the sidebar's tree of a project's folders with every changed file marked - use it to show what changed in a folder or where files are; a project's page shows a project at a glance - its git state, its configuration, the skills, agents and commands it gives a session, and its agent worktrees - with a button to start a session in it; History is the palette that searches every past session's conversation, and opens over the window, taking the keyboard until the user closes it; Settings is where the user changes how Floti behaves, one section at a time. Paths may be relative to your own folder, and must be under a folder Floti knows. The same tool runs from your shell as `floti desktop open`, with `--json` for its answer as JSON.

tools.name: desktop_open
tools.description: Opens one of Floti's views for the user, beside your session's tab, without taking the keyboard from your terminal. view "file" opens a file's tab (path, and line to scroll to); "folder" points the Files view at the project holding a folder, with that folder opened and its changed files marked (path); "project" opens the page of the project holding path; "history" opens the History palette with search typed into it, over the window and with the keyboard until the user closes it; "settings" opens a Settings tab on a section. A relative path is resolved against your own folder, and a path under no folder Floti knows (a workspace or project it found, a profile's folder, or a running session's folder) is refused and nothing opens. Use it when the user asks to see something, such as "show me the code you just wrote" or "show me what you changed".

path.description: For file, folder and project: the file or folder, absolute or relative to your own folder.

line.description: For file: the line to scroll to, counted from 1.

search.description: For history: what to search the past sessions for.

section.description: For settings: the section to open on. Without one, Settings opens where the user last left it.
